newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW-Thailand's Bang Pakong sees revenue up.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Thailand's Bang Pakong sees revenue up.

text.p: Thai industrial park developer, Bang Pakong Industrial Park 2 Plc, said on Wednesday it expected to see rising revenue from its units this year following the completion of their overseas and domestic projects.
"Our units will begin to generate revenue for us this year. Some of our units' new projects have been completed and been opened for sale," its president Vikrom Kromadit told Reuters in an interview.

Bang Pakong is a joint venture between the two Thai Kromadit and Phanichewa families and Japan's Itochu Corporation with 25, 13 and 22 percent stake respectively. The remainder is held by several other minority shareholders.
The firm operates and manages "Bang Pakong Industrial Park" in Chachoengsao province, 75 km (47 miles) east of Bangkok, .
Bang Pakong also owns 87 percent stake in Amata City Co Ltd which is developing an industrial estate in Rayong province known as "Amata City Industrial Park".
Amata City Industrial Park is scheduled to be completed by the middle of this year.
Amata City is also developing an industrial estate in Vietnam in Dong Nai province, close to Ho Chi Minh city known as Amata City (Bien Hoa).
"Our industrial park in Vietnam is okay. About 30 percent of the first phase has already been sold," Vikrom said.
Bien Hoa project will cover a total of some 700 hectares of land. The first phase was completed early this year and covers about 100 hectares, he said.
Amata City has a 54 stake in the Amata City (Bien Hoa) project and the rest is owned by a Vietnam industrial estate agency.
Bang Pakong also holds 39 percent in Amata Power Co Ltd which is building a 170 megawatt power plant in Bang Pakong Industrial Park.
Amata Power will generate electricity for sale to factories in the industrial park and the state-owned Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand under the Small Power Producers (SPP) scheme.
Bang Pakong plans to list on the Stock Exchange of Thailand by offering 21.7 million new shares to the public.
The company on Wednesday cut its initial public offering price of its new shares to 18 baht ($0.70) from 20 baht previously announced.
The reduction in the IPO price was aimed at attracting retail investors amid a bearish mood prevailing in the stock market, Vikrom said.
Bang Pakong is scheduled to make a public offering of its new shares between June 11-13.
Vikrom said Bang Pakong does not have liquidity problems like other property firms because the company tried to avoid owning excessive land banks which would result in high interest expenses.
"Other property companies face liquidity problems because they have to pay a lot of interest for their acquisition of land banks. We don't have that problem," Vikrom said
